To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the supply of apprenticeship was highly flexible in the British Industrial revolution, in the sense that tuition increased slightly in response to changes in the number of new apprentices and returned to its equilibrium level in the short run.

the standard supply of human capital elasticity was high, the tuition increased only marginally in response to increases of the annual number of apprentice, and that the system as a while was able to adapt to changes in the number of new apprentices.

the supply of apprenticeship was very responsive to changes in the demand for apprenticeship, and that this responsiveness was not limited to particular trades but was a feature of the system as whole.

the response of the human capital supply to demand shocks during the British Industrial Revolution and the implications of this response on the Industrial Revolution.
